title: Jobs stay pending forever: no worker claims and AWS Batch fallback does not fire
description:
## Observed

Jobs submitted to the demo API are accepted and then stay `pending`
indefinitely. Nothing ever claims them.

- Content hash `2caf28aa` (home page pitch): `POST /jobs` returned `201`,
  and `{"status": "pending", "audio_url": null}` was still the response
  40+ minutes later.
- Content hash `01355d8a` (an earlier wording of the same pitch): `201`,
  then `pending` for the full 7 minutes it was polled.

Pre-existing hashes such as `31491bc9` (Gettysburg) return `done` with a
signed URL, so the job API, storage, and signed delivery all work. Only
the *production* of new audio is affected.

## Expected

Per the architecture: a local worker races to claim the job, and if nobody
claims it within the configured window, a workflow submits an AWS Batch
GPU job. With no local worker running, the Batch fallback should take the
job. Either path should move it out of `pending`.

Forty minutes with no state change means the fallback is not firing at
all — this is the "AWS safety net" the site advertises.

## Impact

Any new text on any page is permanently silent. Only hashes that were
baked previously can play. The home page demo cannot speak until this is
resolved.

Content-hash dedup means this needs to succeed exactly once per hash: a
single successful render of `2caf28aa` makes the home page demo audible
permanently.

## Gherkin

```gherkin
Feature: Cloud fallback produces audio when no local worker is available
  Scenario: No local worker claims the job
    Given no local worker is claiming jobs
    And a job has been pending past the configured claim timeout
    When the fallback workflow runs
    Then an AWS Batch GPU job is submitted for that job
    And the job status leaves "pending"
```
